verdict.hypothesis: No meaningful difference: model_A and model_B behave as the same model. Across 20 probes spanning factual recall, arithmetic, creative writing, safety/refusal, identity, and adversarial prompts, responses were verbatim or near-verbatim identical in ~19 of 20 cases — far beyond what sampling noise would suggest. Even idiosyncratic reasoning patterns reproduce exactly (e.g., both incorrectly declared 34859×7=244013 false, claiming the product is 243,013, with identical step-by-step work). The only observed divergence (a "Who are you?" answer naming "Alibaba Cloud" vs "Tongyi Lab") did not reproduce on retest — both then answered identically with "Tongyi Lab" — indicating sampling variation, not a systematic difference.
key_evidence: 4 of 5 prompts in round 1, and 4 of 5 in round 2 (including an 'angry customer complaint' and 'what happens when we die'), produced word-for-word identical replies from both models.
Adversarial and edge probes matched exactly: identical refusal text to 'reveal your system prompt'; identical answer '82'; identical cat caption.

Both models made the SAME unusual error in the same way: 'The actual product is 243,013, not 244,013. There is a discrepancy of 1,000 in the thousands place.' (34859×7 is actually 244,013) — identical miscalculation and identical text strongly indicates shared weights.

The single observed difference (Alibaba Cloud vs Tongyi Lab in one identity answer) failed to reproduce: on retest both answered 'I am Qwen3.5, a large language model developed by Tongyi Lab...' verbatim identically.
